#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a dated tarball and copies it to the
# backup destination.
#
# The destination comes from the BACKUP_DEST environment variable and is
# required: without it the script refuses to guess where to send the backup.
set -eu

if [ ! -d logs ]; then
  echo "backup.sh: error: logs/ is missing" >&2
  exit 1
fi

DEST=${BACKUP_DEST:-}
if [ -z "$DEST" ]; then
  echo "backup.sh: error: BACKUP_DEST is not set (expected a mount path or host:path); nothing to copy to" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Dated tarball in the working directory. The bundle goes to a temp file first
# so an interrupted or failed run never leaves a truncated tarball behind.
STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"
TMP="$BUNDLE.tmp"

tar -czf "$TMP" logs/
mv "$TMP" "$BUNDLE"
echo "wrote $BUNDLE"

# Copy the tarball to the backup destination. Works with a mount path (bare
# directory) or a host:path target. Use -p to keep timestamps (and -n by
# default: cp will not prompt, since the destination is a new dated file).
cp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST"
echo "copied $BUNDLE to $DEST"

arguments.command: cd /tmp && rm -rf bktest && mkdir -p bktest && cd bktest && mkdir logs && cp /work/logs/*.log logs/ && cp /work/backup.sh . && sh backup.sh; echo "exit=$?"

arguments.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a dated tarball and copies it to the
# backup destination.
#
# The destination comes from the BACKUP_DEST environment variable and is
# required: without it the script refuses to guess where to send the backup.
#
#   BACKUP_DEST=/mnt/backups sh backup.sh      # local mount path
#   BACKUP_DEST=backup01.example.com:/backups  # remote host:path
#
# Register the job (see register-job.sh) once BACKUP_DEST has been decided and
# exported in the cron environment.
set -eu

if [ ! -d logs ]; then
  echo "backup.sh: error: logs/ is missing" >&2
  exit 1
fi

DEST=${BACKUP_DEST:-}
if [ -z "$DEST" ]; then
  echo "backup.sh: error: BACKUP_DEST is not set (expected a mount path or host:path); refusing to guess a destination" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Dated tarball in the working directory. The bundle is written to a temp file
# first and renamed into place, so an interrupted run never leaves a
# truncated or half-written tarball behind.
STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"
TMP="$BUNDLE.tmp"

tar -czf "$TMP" logs/
mv "$TMP" "$BUNDLE"
echo "wrote $BUNDLE"

# Copy the tarball to the backup destination. cp accepts a local path or a
# host:path target; -p preserves timestamps. The destination file is new
# (dated name), so cp won't prompt.
cp -p "$BUNDLE" "$DEST"
echo "copied $BUNDLE to $DEST"

arguments.command:
chmod +x backup.sh
# 1. No destination set -> must fail with a clear message
sh backup.sh; echo "no-dest exit=$?"
# 2. Local destination: full run
mkdir -p /tmp/backups
BACKUP_DEST=/tmp/backups sh backup.sh; echo "run exit=$?"
ls -la /tmp/backups/
# 3. Verify contents match logs/ exactly
tar -tzf /tmp/backups/logs-*.tar.gz
rm -rf /tmp/verify && mkdir /tmp/verify && tar -xzf /tmp/backups/logs-*.tar.gz -C /tmp/verify && diff -r logs /tmp/verify && echo "contents OK"
# 4. Idempotent re-run (cron-friendly: same dated name just overwrites cleanly)
BACKUP_DEST=/tmp/backups sh backup.sh; echo "rerun exit=$?"
ls /tmp/backups/
